feature: Default domain policy denies Python standard-library I/O
description: The domain import policy `hexa init` scaffolds denies Python's standard-library I/O modules, as it already does for Rust, TypeScript and Go, and still allows pure modules.

specs.description: A Python domain module importing subprocess is denied by the scaffolded policy
specs.given: A project whose rules file is the template `hexa init` writes, and a Python file in the domain layer
specs.when: The file imports `subprocess` and the policy `domain-imports-only-what-it-is-allowed` judges that standard-library import
specs.then: The verdict is a denial naming the `subprocess` entry, and the grade no longer holds

specs.description: Each newly listed Python module appears under a `# Python` heading in the template's deny list
specs.then: Its deny list contains `subprocess`, `socket`, `shutil`, `tempfile`, `glob`, `sqlite3`, `urllib.request`, `ftplib`, `smtplib`, `poplib`, `imaplib`, `ssl`, `signal`, `multiprocessing`, `ctypes` and `importlib`, placed under a `# Python` comment heading

specs.description: A submodule of a listed module is denied on the `.` boundary
specs.given: The scaffolded policy and a Python domain file
specs.then: Each import is denied, because each is the listed module or lies below it on a `.` boundary

specs.description: `os` and `http` already listed for other languages deny Python's os and http modules
specs.given: The scaffolded policy and a Python domain file
specs.then: Each import is denied by the existing `os` or `http` entry

specs.description: `os` and `http` are not listed a second time for Python
specs.when: The entries in its deny list are counted
specs.then: `os` appears exactly once and `http` appears exactly once; the `# Python` section does not repeat either

specs.description: A module that only shares a prefix with a listed name is not denied
specs.given: The scaffolded policy and a Python domain file
specs.when: The file imports a standard-library-origin name such as `signals` or `globals_helper` that is not `signal`/`glob` nor below them on a `.` boundary
specs.then: The import is not denied by the `signal` or `glob` entries

specs.description: A listed Python I/O import in a domain file never passes
specs.given: The scaffolded policy and a Python domain file importing `socket`
specs.then: The verdict is not a pass

specs.description: Every listed Python module and every module below it is denied
specs.given: The scaffolded policy, any module M from {subprocess, socket, shutil, tempfile, glob, sqlite3, urllib.request, ftplib, smtplib, poplib, imaplib, ssl, signal, multiprocessing, ctypes, importlib, os, http}, and any suffix S of `.`-separated identifiers (possibly empty)
specs.when: A Python domain file imports `M` or `M.S` from the standard library

specs.description: Pure standard-library modules pass in the domain
specs.given: The scaffolded policy and a Python domain file
The scaffolded policy and a Python domain file
specs.then: The import passes; only `urllib.request` and what lies below it is denied

specs.description: The template does not list pure modules, nor `urllib` as a whole
A standard-library import no deny entry covers always passes
specs.given: The scaffolded policy and any Python standard-library module name N that is neither a listed entry nor below one on a `.` boundary
specs.when: A Python domain file imports N

specs.description: Rust, TypeScript and Go entries are unchanged
specs.given: The scaffolded template before and after this ADR
specs.when: The deny entries outside the `# Python` section are compared
specs.then: They are the same entries as before, and a Rust domain file importing `std::fs` or a Go domain file importing `os/exec` is judged exactly as before

specs.description: Third-party Python packages are not denied by default
specs.given: The scaffolded policy and a Python domain file
specs.when: The file imports a third-party package such as `requests` or `sqlalchemy`
specs.then: No entry added by this ADR denies it; the template's deny list names no third-party package

specs.description: An existing project's rules file is not rewritten
specs.given: A Python project whose rules file was written before this ADR, with a deny list lacking `subprocess`
specs.when: The project is analyzed after this change
specs.then: Its own deny list is used unchanged, so a domain import of `subprocess` is not denied by it, and the file is not modified

specs.description: The change only adds Python standard-library entries
specs.given: The deny list of the template before this ADR (B) and after (A)
specs.then: B is a subset of A, and every entry in A not in B is one of the sixteen Python standard-library modules §1 names
